status_detail: Intensive two-pass review published 38 exact SHA-256 executable artifacts from CERT Polska's 2026-09-23 reverse-engineering report on a coordinated and continuing Android toll-fraud campaign. CERT Polska reconstructed the infection chain with static analysis, controlled Android 15 execution, network inspection, decrypted C2 exchanges, and observed live premium-SMS and carrier-billing tasking; its indicator set was observed or recovered 2026-09-14 through 2026-09-21. The over-10 single-operation exception is justified by the report's major campaign scope: 17 code- or infrastructure-confirmed malicious apps, 852 linked ads, multiple loaders and payload stages, and operational C2 after store removal. Daily-Threat-Intel supplied only domains and IPs. Forty-six fresh MalwareBazaar browse candidates were held because the human-verification checkpoint and API authentication prevented access to metadata-rich individual records; bare browse labels were not accepted. The CERT Polska pass reviewed 57 executable/non-executable hash candidates, accepted 38 executable APK/DEX/SO/JS artifacts, and rejected 19 configuration splits, signer/source-stamp certificates, advertising files, and APKs lacking code confirmation. CERT Orange independently corroborated the campaign context on 2026-09-28 but did not name exact SHA-256s, so exact-hash independent-corroboration metrics remain zero.
